critical_code_review_comments: radar.py uses `asyncio.create_task(run_for_user(...))` fire-and-forget on the FastAPI event loop. If the worker is killed mid-run, the task is orphaned; the `interrompue` recovery in ensure_radar_indexes handles stale 'running' rows at startup — good — but there is no heartbeat, so a crashed-but-still-marked-running task will block /run for 15 minutes (the busy window). Consider a stricter 'last heartbeat' column.

radar.py `/run` 15-minute busy window: a legitimate long run (e.g. 20+ new offers at ~5s each with sem=4) may fit, but if a user packs many offers simultaneously the ThreadPool can get saturated. Semaphore(4) is a sensible cap.
radar.py dashboard builds `top_a`/`top_b` by scanning up to 400 offers in memory and sorting in Python — fine for small volumes; add an index on (user_id, ips.score) once scale grows.
radar.py `cron` endpoint deduplicates users via a list membership check (`if p['user_id'] not in users`) which is O(n²) over users; use a set.

followup.py build_ics escapes semicolons/commas/newlines correctly but does not fold lines at 75 octets as per RFC 5545 — most calendar clients tolerate it, but strict parsers (some corporate Outlook policies) may reject >75 char lines.
Followup.jsx `email-mark-sent` relies on `window.confirm` — works but not stylable; consider a shadcn AlertDialog for consistency.

Radar.jsx `datetime-local` input in Followup.jsx is the browser-native picker (not shadcn Calendar). Matches the earlier design-review guidance for the Suivi tab since it is a time input, but note the mismatch with other date pickers in the app.

RadarSettings.jsx uses `defaultValue={csv(s.keywords)}` with onBlur — state updates only when the user leaves the field; if a member types then clicks 'Enregistrer' directly, the blur fires in time in Chrome but Safari sometimes drops it. Prefer value/onChange or key the form on `s`.
